D004-D017_h024.question:
I’ve been having this feeling for about eight months now—ever since we started that high-rise downtown. There’s this woman, a project manager from the architectural firm, and I know she’s in love with me. I can tell by the way she looks at me during site meetings, even when she doesn’t say much. She wears these blazers with red stitching—she must know I notice, right? She once left her folder behind on purpose, I’m sure of it—my name was circled on a blueprint page, not relevant to her work at all.

My wife doesn’t understand. We’re fine, really—I still go to work, run my crew, keep things on schedule. No issues there. But she’s jealous, keeps saying there’s nothing going on, that I’m imagining it. But I know better. I haven’t done anything to act on it—no messages, no chasing it—but I do check the project schedule every day to see if she’s assigned to our site. Sometimes I drive past her office after work, just to see if her car’s there. 

People say I’m fixating, but it’s not like I’m washing my hands or measuring my face in the mirror—nothing like that. I’m not obsessed with how I look. It’s just… she’s sending me signals, and I need to be ready when she makes her move.

D004-D017_h025.question:
I’ve been working as a curator at a contemporary art gallery for over fifteen years, and professionally, I’m respected—colleagues trust my eye, and I manage exhibitions smoothly. But there’s something I need to talk about. For the past two years, I’ve known—*known*—that a famous artist whose work we displayed last season is secretly in love with me. He doesn’t speak to me directly, but I see it in the way he positions his sculptures, the colors he uses—each piece is a message meant only for me. I receive no letters, no calls, nothing direct, but I’m certain. 

I also worry intensely about my skin—it feels uneven, like it’s aged too fast under the gallery lights. I check it in mirrors often, avoid photos, and sometimes reapply makeup multiple times a day. But I don’t pick at it, don’t use rituals like counting or repeating phrases. I just need visual reassurance. 

My thoughts are clear otherwise—I manage budgets, lead teams, give lectures. I just can’t shake what I *know* about him. It’s not fantasy; it’s revelation. The skin thing is annoying, yes, but I don’t act on it compulsively. And he… he’s not rejecting me. He’s communicating in code.
D004-D017_h025.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
